title: Microsoft Teams: Copilot in the Queues app on mobile
summary: Hold for a qualification in the licence-assignment guidance: the stated Microsoft Entra role requirement applies to delegated Graph requests, not every request. The rollout, licensing prerequisites, control paths and commands otherwise match the supplied notice and Microsoft documentation.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate feature price, meter or Copilot Credits charge is stated in the supplied records and relevant Learn documentation.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app Copilot credits licensing; Queues app mobile Copilot licensing credits meter. Read roadmap, MC1552391, manage-queues-app, Teams add-on licensing, Copilot Teams calling and release-note excerpts; no feature-specific meter or price.

claims.claim: After Teams Premium assignment, the Queues app can take up to 48 hours to appear.
claims.quote: Once a user is licensed for Teams Premium, it can take up to 48 hours for Queues app to be available in the Teams client.

claims.claim: The Queues app is enabled by default for voice-enabled Teams users assigned both Teams Premium and Teams Phone.
claims.quote: Queues app is enabled by default for all Teams users in your organization who are assigned both a Teams Premium and Teams Phone license and who are voice enabled.

claims.claim: The Queues app documentation lists iOS and Android mobile clients as supported.
claims.quote: The Queues app is currently supported on Teams desktop, Mac, and Virtualized Desktop Infrastructure (VDI) clients, Teams phones (touch devices only), and iOS and Android mobile clients.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The feature does not change how recordings are created, stored or accessed.
claims.quote: This feature does not change how call recordings are created, stored, or accessed.

claims.claim: Copilot in the Queues app is already available on desktop.
claims.quote: Copilot in the Queues app is already available on desktop, and Mobile brings the same capability to the phone.

claims.claim: The October 27, 2026 release notes describe opening a recorded Queues call from unified call history and launching the Copilot Chat sidecar from Recap.
claims.quote: October 27, 2026; Use Copilot Chat after a call in Queues app [Windows, Mac]; Navigate to the unified call history in the Queues app, select the recorded call record, and launch the Copilot Chat sidecar from within the Recap tab.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has no dedicated page for this mobile feature at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues app" "Copilot" "mobile"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Copilot" "Queues". Opened manage-queues-app and copilot-teams-calling-transcription; read release-note search excerpts describing desktop, not a dedicated mobile page.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Representatives' recording-access selection cannot be changed after an automatic recording template is created.
claims.quote: Select which call recordings call queue representatives (agents) can access. Authorized users have access by default. This setting can't be modified once the template is created.

claims.claim: An automatic recording template determines the SharePoint storage location for recordings and transcripts and access to recordings.
claims.quote: An automatic recording template for Call Queue defines where, in SharePoint, recordings and transcripts will be stored, the prompts played to callers to let them know that recording is enabled, and defines who has access to the recordings.

claims.claim: General Copilot interactions are logged automatically when auditing is enabled.
claims.quote: The system automatically logs these activities as part of Audit (Standard). If your organization enables auditing, you don't need to take extra steps to configure auditing support for Copilot and AI applications.

claims.claim: General Copilot audit logs are accessible and searchable under Audit in the Microsoft Purview portal.
claims.quote: Access Copilot audit logs by using the Microsoft Purview portal and selecting Audit. To search for specific Copilot or AI application scenarios, use the Activities – operation names field

claims.claim: General retention policies for AI apps include Microsoft 365 Copilot prompts and responses.
claims.quote: Retention policies for AI apps include user prompts and responses for Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio

claims.claim: General generative-AI message data is stored in a hidden folder in the user's mailbox.
claims.quote: Data from generative AI messages is stored in a hidden folder in the mailbox of the user who runs the AI app.

claims.claim: Messages in these hidden mailbox folders are searchable with eDiscovery.
claims.quote: Messages stored in mailboxes, including the hidden folders, are searchable by eDiscovery tools.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not separately confirmed how these audit and retention behaviours apply to Copilot in the Queues app on mobile.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues app" "Copilot" "audit" "retention". Opened audit-copilot and retention-policies-copilot and searched audit text for Queues; neither identifies this mobile experience or an experience-specific exception.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not describe a separate permission for Copilot in the Queues app.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app mobile Copilot enable disable policy permission PowerShell Graph licensing credits meter; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Copilot" "Queues". Read manage-queues-app, Copilot calling documentation and Queues release-note excerpts.

claims.claim: The supplied records describe answering questions and surfacing insights, not Copilot acting autonomously.
claims.quote: Understand a customer conversation and decide on a follow-up without reviewing the full call.

claims.claim: The automatic recording setup page requires Shared Call History on the call queue.
claims.quote: Shared Call History in enabled on the call queue. With Shared Call History enabled, authorized users and representatives (agents) will be able to access the recordings and transcriptons through Queues App.

claims.claim: Explicit recording consent must be Off for automatic recording.
claims.quote: Explicit recording consent must be Off.

claims.claim: Licence assignment is at Microsoft 365 admin center > Billing > Licenses > product > Assign licenses.
claims.quote: In the admin center, go to the Billing > Licenses page. Select a product. On the product details page, select Assign licenses.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense is the Graph endpoint for assigning or removing user licences.
claims.quote: Add or remove licenses for the user to enable or disable their use of Microsoft cloud offerings; POST /users/{id | userPrincipalName}/assignLicense; POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/me/assignLicense

claims.claim: The Graph call needs a supported Microsoft Entra role such as License Administrator or User Administrator.
claims.quote: In delegated scenarios with work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role with the microsoft.directory/users/assignLicense role permission.
claims.fix: Replace the note's second sentence with: 'For delegated Graph requests, the signed-in user needs a supported Microsoft Entra role such as License Administrator or User Administrator, or a custom role with microsoft.directory/users/assignLicense. Application requests use application permissions; LicenseAssignment.ReadWrite.All is the least privileged.' Keep https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/user-assignlicense as the source.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: The automatic recording template assignment path is Teams admin center > Voice > Call queue > call queue > Templates > Automatic recording template.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Voice > Call queue. Select the call queue you want to have automatic recording for. On the Templates tab, scroll to find the Automatic recording template section.

claims.claim: Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid> -AutoRecordingTemplateId <String> applies an automatic recording template to a queue.
claims.quote: Set-CsCallQueue -Identity <Guid>; [-AutoRecordingTemplateId <String>]; The AutoRecordingTemplateId parameter indicates the Auto Recording template to apply to the call queue.

claims.claim: The Set-CsCallQueue reference restricts AutoRecordingTemplateId to Voice applications private preview customers.
claims.quote: -AutoRecordingTemplateId; Voice applications private preview customers only.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference says saving the queue through Teams admin center removes that parameter's setting.
claims.quote: Saving a call queue configuration through Teams admin center will remove this setting.

claims.claim: Automatic recording templates are created under Teams admin center > Voice > Templates and resources.
claims.quote: In the Teams admin center, go to Voice > Templates and resources. Select Templates. Select Automatic Recording as the template type. Select Add to create a new Automatic Recording template.

claims.claim: The setup page's August 13, 2026 entry says automatic recording for call queues can be configured through PowerShell.
claims.quote: August 13, 2026; Automatic Recording for Call Queue can be configured via PowerShell.

claims.claim: The general Teams calling Copilot control is at Teams admin center > Voice > Calling policies > policy > Copilot.
claims.quote: Under Voice, select Calling policies. Either select an existing policy or create a new one. From the dropdown for the Copilot setting, select On, On with saved transcript required, or Off.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled turns off Copilot under the general calling policy.
claims.quote: To turn off Copilot for calls, use the following command: Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy -Identity <policy name> -Copilot Disabled

claims.claim: The general calling policy documentation covers one-to-one and group calls and identifies 1:1 Teams and PSTN calls.
claims.quote: APPLIES TO: 1:1 Teams calls; Public Switched Telephone Network (PSTN) calls. Teams calling policies control Copilot in one-to-one and group calls.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Governance controls notes; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the general calling Copilot policy governs Copilot in the Queues app.
claims.quote: Searched: "Queues" "Copilot" "policy"; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Queues" "Copilot" "disable". Read copilot-teams-calling-transcription, manage-queues-app, Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy and Queues release-note excerpts; no explicit applicability.

claims.claim: The documented org-wide app control is Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps.
claims.quote: Navigate to Teams apps > Manage apps. Select Actions > Org-wide app settings > Microsoft apps. Select Off and Save.

claims.claim: An API or automation equivalent for the documented org-wide Microsoft apps switch is not documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app org-wide Microsoft apps settings disable PowerShell Graph API; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell "Org-wide app settings" "Microsoft apps". Read manage-queues-app and returned CustomApp cmdlet excerpts, which concern custom app sideloading.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls notes
claims.claim: Turning off the Queues app through that org-wide setting also turns off Insights and Tasks rather than only Copilot.
claims.quote: You can turn off the Queues app via the Teams admin center. However, doing so also turns off other Microsoft apps like Insights and Tasks.

claims.where: controls[4]; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: No separate UI or API tenant switch for Copilot in the Queues app on mobile is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Queues app mobile Copilot enable disable policy permission PowerShell Graph; site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams "Queues" "Copilot" "disable". Read manage-queues-app, Copilot calling policy page, Set-CsTeamsCallingPolicy and release-note excerpts.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends confirming automatic recording is on for the queues where users should use Copilot.
claims.quote: Confirm that automatic recording is turned on for the call queues where you want users to use Copilot.

claims.claim: The notice recommends aligning Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams Premium assignments for intended users, expressed here as an instruction to assign them.
claims.quote: Review Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams Premium license assignments for the users who will use the feature.
claims.fix: Replace the first checklist bullet with: 'Review Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams Premium licence assignments for intended users, as Microsoft's notice recommends. Assign missing licences where appropriate and confirm users also hold Teams Phone (licence assignment row).' This separates Microsoft's recommendation to review from the wiki's advice to assign.
